title: Forced Cotton Cultivation Expands in Northern Mozambique
note: Coercive cotton cultivation system in colonial Mozambique is well-documented by UNU-WIDER and Cambridge Core; ran from 1926 to 1961 with peak exploitation in northern regions.

title: Mozambique Reclassified as Overseas Province
note: Portuguese parliament approved reclassification on June 11, 1951 via constitutional amendment; framing as UN-avoidance maneuver confirmed by multiple sources.

title: South African Migrant Labor Convention Renewed
note: The Mozambique-South Africa migrant labor arrangement (via WNLA) is well-documented throughout the 1950s, but no source confirms a specific 1952 renewal. The broader system is verified; the specific 1952 renewal date is not.

title: Dock Workers Strike in Lourenco Marques Suppressed
note: A 1956 dock workers strike is documented in Portuguese Guinea (Bissau), not Mozambique. No source confirms a 1956 dock strike in Lourenco Marques specifically. The famous 1959 Pidjiguiti massacre was in Guinea-Bissau. Event may be confabulated or mislocated.

title: Mueda Massacre — Troops Fire on Petitioning Villagers
note: Confirmed: June 16, 1960 massacre of Makonde petitioners in Cabo Delgado; death toll disputed (30–600); foundational event for FRELIMO's formation. Widely documented.

title: FRELIMO Founded in Dar es Salaam
note: Founded June 25, 1962 in Dar es Salaam by merger of MANU, UDENAMO, UNAMI under Eduardo Mondlane's presidency. All details confirmed.

title: FRELIMO Launches Armed Struggle — September 25
note: Attack on Chai administrative post in Cabo Delgado on September 25, 1964 confirmed as official start date; the date is celebrated as Armed Forces Day.

title: FRELIMO President Eduardo Mondlane Assassinated
note: Mondlane was killed on February 3, 1969, not 1968. The year in the event is wrong by one year. All sources consistently confirm 1969. The parcel bomb and PIDE link details are otherwise accurate.

title: Operation Gordian Knot Fails to Crush FRELIMO
note: Confirmed: seven-month 1970 campaign deploying 35,000 troops; destroyed most FRELIMO bases but failed to deliver decisive blow; FRELIMO reconstituted during rainy season.

title: Wiriyamu Massacre — Hundreds of Civilians Killed
note: The Wiriyamu massacre occurred on December 16, 1972, not 1971. The event year is wrong. Death toll (150–385) and exposure via Spanish missionaries in 1973 are confirmed, but the year 1971 is incorrect.

title: Portugal's Carnation Revolution Ends Colonial Wars
note: April 25, 1974 coup confirmed; Lusaka Accord signed September 7, 1974 setting June 25, 1975 independence date. All details accurate.

title: Mozambique Achieves Independence — June 25
note: June 25, 1975 independence with Samora Machel as first president confirmed; ~250,000 Portuguese settlers fled; one-party Marxist-Leninist state declared. All details verified.

title: Mozambique Closes Border with Rhodesia — Absorbs Retaliation
note: Machel announced border closure March 3, 1976 to implement UN sanctions; Rhodesia retaliated by supporting RENAMO formation. All details confirmed.

title: RENAMO Founded With Rhodesian Intelligence Support
note: Confirmed: founded May 1977 with Rhodesian CIO sponsorship from disaffected anti-FRELIMO elements. Some sources give 1976 for initial recruitment; formal adoption of RENAMO name in May 1977 confirmed.

title: South Africa Takes Over RENAMO Sponsorship
note: After Zimbabwe independence in 1980, South African military intelligence assumed RENAMO sponsorship. All details about ANC operations and destabilization strategy confirmed.

title: Famine Threatens Millions as War and Drought Combine
note: Severe drought combined with RENAMO disruption created famine conditions in early-to-mid 1980s; the specific figure of three million affected is not pinpointed to 1983 alone but the general event is confirmed by HRW and other sources.

title: Nkomati Accord — Non-Aggression Pact with South Africa
note: Signed March 16, 1984 by Machel and P.W. Botha. South Africa continued supplying RENAMO in violation; Gorongosa documents confirmed this. All details accurate.

title: Mozambique Joins the IMF and World Bank
note: Mozambique joined the IMF on September 24, 1984, not 1985. The event year is incorrect by one year. The shift from socialist to market-oriented policy is correctly described.

title: President Samora Machel Killed in Mbuzini Plane Crash
note: October 19, 1986 crash at Mbuzini confirmed; 34 deaths (not 34 others — Machel plus 33 others); South African false-beacon theory investigated but not conclusively proven. Minor discrepancy: 33 others died alongside Machel (34 total), the event says '34 others' which is one over.

title: Economic Rehabilitation Program Launched Under IMF
note: ERP launched in 1987 confirmed by IMF and World Bank archives; SAF arrangement supported program until 1990; currency, price, and civil service reforms all documented.

title: Homoine Massacre — RENAMO Kills Hundreds of Civilians
note: The Homoine massacre occurred on July 18, 1987, not 1988. Death toll of 424 confirmed including hospital patients. The year in the event is wrong.

title: FRELIMO Abandons Marxism-Leninism at Fifth Congress
note: At the 5th Party Congress in 1989, FRELIMO formally dropped Marxism-Leninism and class struggle; opened party to all social categories. All details confirmed.

title: New Constitution Establishes Multiparty Democracy
note: Constitution approved November 2, 1990 and came into force November 30, 1990. Established multiparty democracy, eliminated FRELIMO's leading role, renamed country. All details confirmed.

title: General Peace Agreement Ends 16-Year Civil War
note: Signed October 4, 1992 in Rome by Chissano and Dhlakama; ~1 million deaths confirmed; October 4 is Peace Day. All details accurate.

title: ONUMOZ UN Peacekeeping Mission Manages Demobilization
note: ONUMOZ established December 1992, operational 1993; demobilized ~91,000 fighters total (67,042 government + 24,648 RENAMO), not 75,000 as stated. $500M cost and success framing confirmed.

title: First Multiparty Elections — Chissano Wins Presidency
note: Elections October 27-29, 1994; Chissano 53.3%, Dhlakama 33.7%; FRELIMO 129 seats, RENAMO 119 seats. Event says RENAMO won 112 seats — actual figure is 119. Minor inaccuracy but core facts verified.

title: Mozambique Joins the Commonwealth of Nations
note: Mozambique joined November 13, 1995 as the first country without historical British ties. All details confirmed.

title: Rapid Economic Growth Returns After War Destruction
note: GDP growth averaged 10% annually 1996-98 per IMF; poverty reduction lag also documented. All claims confirmed.

title: Mozal Aluminum Smelter — Landmark Foreign Investment
note: Project launched/announced 1997-1998; BHP Billiton (via Billiton) led consortium; first production 2000-2001. Event says 'began production in 2001' — production started September 2000. Minor date variance but core facts verified.

title: HIPC Debt Relief Milestone for Mozambique
note: IMF/World Bank agreed Mozambique eligible for HIPC in April 1998; completion point June 1999; total relief ~$3.7 billion. One of the largest HIPC operations. All details confirmed.

title: Catastrophic Floods Devastate Southern Mozambique
note: Floods February-March 2000 caused by Cyclone Leon-Eline; ~800 deaths, ~500,000 displaced; baby Rosita rescued from tree by South African helicopter — iconic image confirmed.

title: Investigative Journalist Carlos Cardoso Murdered
note: Shot dead November 22, 2000 in Maputo; investigating $14M BCM bank fraud; Nyimpine Chissano (son of former president) charged. All details confirmed.

title: Pande-Temane Gas Fields Begin Exports to South Africa
note: Pipeline completed 2003, gas exports to South Africa started 2004; led by Sasol; Pande field brought on production 2009, Temane 2004. Event assigns year 2003 which matches pipeline completion. Confirmed.

title: Armando Guebuza Elected President
note: Guebuza won with 63.7%; RENAMO's Dhlakama received 31-33% (event says 31%). Low turnout ~36% confirmed. All core details verified.

title: Mozambique Acquires 85% Stake in Cahora Bassa Dam
note: Agreement implemented in 2006; Mozambique purchased 67% equity bringing stake from 18% to 85%; $250M paid from state budget plus $700M loan. All details confirmed.

title: Anadarko and ENI Acquire Rovuma Basin Exploration Blocks
note: Blocks were awarded in 2006, not 2008; Anadarko conducted seismic surveys in 2008, but the block acquisitions predate this. The 2008 date does not match the block award timeline. Event year is inaccurate for the described event.

title: September Food Price Riots Kill Thirteen in Maputo
note: September 1-2, 2010 riots against 30% bread price rise; death toll reports vary (10-13); police fired live rounds; government reversed price increases. All core details confirmed.

title: Rovuma Basin Confirmed as World-Class Gas Province
note: Anadarko confirmed major discovery November 2010 (first well December 2009); ENI confirmed Area 4 finds; combined estimates exceeded 100 tcf. All details confirmed.

title: Coal Mining Boom Begins in Tete Province
note: Vale began coal production at Moatize May 2011; Rio Tinto acquired Riversdale (Benga mine) April 2011; community displacement and human rights criticism documented by HRW. All details confirmed.

title: RENAMO Resumes Low-Level Armed Activity
note: RENAMO began retraining veterans in October 2012 and Dhlakama withdrew to Gorongosa, but confirmed armed attacks (police station, military patrols) began April 2013. The insurgency Wikipedia article is titled 2013-2021. The 2012 mobilization is confirmed but the event's framing of resumed 'attacks' fits 2013 better.

title: Filipe Nyusi Elected as Mozambique's Third President
note: Elections October 15, 2014; Nyusi won 57%; Dhlakama 36.6%; September ceasefire enabled elections. Nyusi described as third president is accurate (Machel, Chissano, Guebuza preceded him).

title: Tuna Bonds Scandal — $2.2 Billion in Hidden State Debt
note: Loans arranged 2013-2014 for EMATUM, Proindicus, MAM via Credit Suisse and VTB; total $2.2B without parliamentary authorization; large portions diverted to arms and corrupt payments. Event dated 2015 (when the loans were being managed/restructured) is slightly off — the core loans were 2013-14, public disclosure 2016. The 2015 year is marginal.

title: Hidden Debt Crisis Triggers Currency Collapse and IMF Suspension
note: IMF suspended program April 2016; metical fell 50%+; Credit Suisse fined ~$500M and forgave $200M of debt. All details confirmed.

title: Islamist Insurgency Emerges in Cabo Delgado
note: First attack October 5, 2017 in Mocimboa da Praia confirmed; group is Ansar al-Sunna (locally called Al-Shabaab, unrelated to Somali group). All details confirmed.

title: RENAMO Leader Afonso Dhlakama Dies
note: Died May 3, 2018 at age 65 in Gorongosa; diabetes-related causes reported; succeeded by Ossufo Momade. All details confirmed.

title: Cyclone Idai Devastates Beira — Africa's Worst Modern Storm
note: Landfall March 14-15 near Beira; 195 km/h winds; ~602 deaths in Mozambique (~1,303 total across 3 countries); 90% of Beira destroyed; $773M damage estimate; Cyclone Kenneth followed weeks later. All details confirmed.

title: RENAMO Peace Agreement Signed — Decentralization Deal
note: Maputo Accord signed August 6, 2019 by Nyusi and Ossufo Momade; direct election of provincial governors; RENAMO demobilization provisions. All details confirmed.

title: TotalEnergies Makes $20 Billion LNG Final Investment Decision
note: The Final Investment Decision was made in June 2019, not 2020. In 2020, TotalEnergies signed a $14.9-15.4B senior debt financing package. The event year and description conflate the 2019 FID with the 2020 financing close.

title: Palma Attack Forces Suspension of Total LNG Project
note: March 24, 2021 Palma attack confirmed; TotalEnergies declared force majeure April 26, 2021 and evacuated all personnel. All details confirmed.

title: Rwanda Deploys Special Forces to Cabo Delgado
note: Rwanda deployed ~1,000 troops; Mocimboa da Praia recaptured August 8, 2021; SAMIM also deployed. Event states 800,000 displaced — actual IDP count exceeded 800,000 by late 2021. All details confirmed.

title: ENI Coral Sul FLNG Produces First Mozambican LNG Cargo
note: First cargo departed November 13, 2022 from Coral Sul FLNG; first FLNG in Africa and first in ultra-deep waters; Area 4 operated by ENI. All details confirmed.

title: Disputed Election Sparks Mass Protests and Over 300 Deaths
note: Chapo declared winner with 71%; Mondlane/PODEMOS disputed; protests and security force crackdown documented. Amnesty International and other sources cite 300-400+ deaths. Constitutional Council upheld Chapo in December. All core details confirmed.

title: Daniel Chapo Inaugurated as Fourth President Amid Unrest
note: Inauguration date January 15, 2025 and ongoing protests are confirmed. However, Chapo is Mozambique's fifth president (Machel, Chissano, Guebuza, Nyusi, Chapo), not fourth as stated. The error is in the ordinal.
